title: Resale listing tool states only what the photo proves and blocks risky claims from publishing
summary: AI listing writers guess brands, sizes and materials, which can get resellers refunded or banned. This open-source tool turns a photo into evidence-backed claims, prices the item from comparable sales, and blocks publishing until high-risk guesses are confirmed.
agent_role: The system extracts per-attribute claims from a photo, classifies each by confidence and visual evidence, prices from comps or abstains, and gates publishing. The seller confirms any unverified attributes manually.
outcome: Author reports that on a 7-item annotated benchmark, unsupported claims fell from 1.14 per listing to 0, while 96% of knowable attributes were kept.
what_they_did: A developer built Honest Lister after a reseller had an item refunded because an AI tool wrongly called it leather. The tool asks an open-weight vision model, for each attribute, what it is, how confident it is and what in the photo shows it. A small classifier then marks each claim observed, inferred, unverified or contradicted. It prices the item from comparable sales or abstains, and refuses to publish while a high-risk claim is unresolved.
how_it_went: The author reports cutting unsupported claims from 1.14 per listing to 0 and raising correct abstention from 47% to 100% on 7 annotated items. It kept 96% of the attributes that were genuinely knowable from the photo.
worth_knowing: Running the 2B model on a laptop CPU took 285 seconds for a single query, so real inference needs a GPU. The hosted demo uses a deterministic backend.
prompt: Look at this photo of a second-hand item I want to sell: [photo]. For each attribute (category, colour, condition, brand, size, material), tell me the value, your confidence, and what in the photo shows it. Treat brand, size and material as unverified unless a label or logo is clearly visible. Then do two things. First, draft a listing using only the well-supported attributes, hedging the uncertain ones. Second, list what I must confirm manually and which extra photo would settle each point. Suggest a price range only if you can find enough comparable sold listings, and tell me the sample size. Do not post anything.

curation.rationale: A multi-step pipeline: vision claims, an evidence ledger, comparable-sales pricing and a publish gate. It comes with code, a demo and a small benchmark. It is closer to a structured LLM pipeline than an autonomous agent, and the benchmark covers only 7 items.
